syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

concepts.learning_objective: Classify halogen compounds by the number of halogen atoms and the hybridisation of the carbon bearing the halogen.
Name haloalkanes and haloarenes by the IUPAC system and identify them as primary, secondary or tertiary.
Distinguish geminal and vicinal dihalides and relate their common and IUPAC names.

topics.title: Nature of the C-X bond and methods of preparation

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the polarity, length and enthalpy of the carbon-halogen bond to the size of the halogen.
Describe the preparation of haloalkanes from alcohols, hydrocarbons and by halogen exchange.
Describe the preparation of haloarenes by electrophilic substitution and from diazonium salts.
Explain the trends in boiling points of haloalkanes with halogen size and branching.
Explain the low water solubility and the density trends of haloalkanes.
Relate the high melting point of para-dihalobenzenes to molecular symmetry.
Predict the products of haloalkanes with ambident nucleophiles such as cyanide and nitrite.
Describe the SN2 mechanism, its kinetics and the effect of steric hindrance on its rate.
Describe the SN1 mechanism and relate its rate to carbocation stability.
Identify chiral molecules and state how enantiomers differ in their properties.
Predict retention, inversion or racemisation at an asymmetric carbon in substitution reactions.

topics.title: Elimination reactions and reactions with metals

concepts.learning_objective: Predict the major alkene in dehydrohalogenation using Zaitsev's rule.
Decide whether substitution or elimination is favoured from the halide and the base.
Describe the formation of Grignard reagents and the Wurtz reaction of alkyl halides.
Explain the low reactivity of haloarenes towards nucleophilic substitution and the effect of nitro groups.
Explain why halogens are deactivating yet ortho, para-directing in electrophilic substitution.
Identify the Wurtz-Fittig and Fittig reactions of aryl halides with sodium.
State the uses and hazards of dichloromethane, chloroform, iodoform and carbon tetrachloride.
Describe freons and explain how they affect the ozone layer.
Explain why DDT persists and accumulates in living organisms.

topics.title: Classification and nomenclature of alcohols, phenols and ethers

concepts.learning_objective: Classify alcohols, phenols and ethers by the number of -OH groups, the hybridisation of the carbon bearing -OH, and the groups on the ether oxygen.
Name alcohols, phenols and ethers by common and IUPAC systems.
Relate the bond angles at oxygen in alcohols and ethers to lone pair and bulky group repulsions.
Explain why the C-O bond in phenol is shorter than in methanol.
Describe preparation of alcohols from alkenes and by reduction of carbonyl compounds and acids.
Predict the class and structure of alcohols formed from Grignard reagents and carbonyl compounds.
Describe preparation of phenol from haloarenes, sulphonic acids, diazonium salts and cumene.

topics.title: Physical properties of alcohols and phenols

concepts.learning_objective: Explain trends in boiling points of alcohols in terms of hydrogen bonding, chain length and branching.
Explain the solubility of alcohols in water and its dependence on the size of the alkyl group.

topics.title: Acidity and esterification of alcohols and phenols

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the acid strength of alcohols, water and substituted phenols using inductive and resonance effects.
Describe esterification of alcohols and phenols and the role of the reagents used.

topics.title: Reactions of alcohols and commercially important alcohols

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the Lucas test and the mechanism and ease of acid-catalysed dehydration of alcohols.
Predict the oxidation and dehydrogenation products of primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols.
Describe the manufacture, uses and toxicity of methanol and ethanol.
Explain nitration and halogenation of phenol in terms of the activating, ortho-para directing -OH group.
Write the products of Kolbe's and Reimer-Tiemann reactions of phenol.
Prepare ethers by dehydration of alcohols and Williamson synthesis and state their limitations.
Explain the physical properties of ethers and their cleavage by hydrogen halides and ring substitution.

topics.title: Nomenclature and structure of the carbonyl group

concepts.learning_objective: Write common and IUPAC names of aldehydes and ketones, including ring and unsaturated compounds.
Describe the hybridisation, geometry and polarity of the carbonyl group.
Choose reagents and named reactions that give aldehydes from alcohols, hydrocarbons, acyl chlorides, nitriles and esters.
Choose methods that give ketones from acyl chlorides, nitriles, alkynes and arenes.

topics.title: Physical properties and uses of aldehydes and ketones

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the boiling points and solubility of aldehydes and ketones in terms of intermolecular forces.
State important uses of common aldehydes and ketones.

topics.title: Nucleophilic addition, reduction and oxidation of aldehydes and ketones

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the mechanism of nucleophilic addition and the relative reactivity of aldehydes and ketones.
Identify reagents that reduce carbonyl compounds to alcohols or to hydrocarbons.
Use oxidation reactions such as Tollens', Fehling's and iodoform tests to distinguish and identify carbonyl compounds.

topics.title: Reactions due to alpha-hydrogen and other reactions

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the alpha-hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones are acidic.
Predict the products of aldol and cross aldol condensation.
Identify aldehydes that undergo the Cannizzaro reaction and predict its products.

topics.title: Carboxylic acids: nomenclature, preparation and physical properties

concepts.learning_objective: Write common and IUPAC names of mono- and dicarboxylic acids.
Choose methods to prepare carboxylic acids from alcohols, alkylbenzenes, nitriles and Grignard reagents.
Explain the boiling points and solubility of carboxylic acids.
Compare the acidity of carboxylic acids with phenols and alcohols using conjugate base stability.
Predict how electron withdrawing and donating groups change the acidity of carboxylic acids.

topics.title: Other reactions and uses of carboxylic acids

concepts.learning_objective: Write reactions that replace the -OH of the carboxyl group to give acid chlorides, esters, anhydrides and amides.
Describe reduction and decarboxylation of carboxylic acids and the reagents used.
Explain the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction and ring substitution in aromatic acids.

topics.title: Structure, classification and nomenclature of amines

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the sp3 hybridisation of nitrogen and the pyramidal shape of amines.
Classify amines as primary, secondary or tertiary from the number of groups on nitrogen.
Name alkylamines and arylamines by common and IUPAC systems.
Explain the reduction of nitro compounds to amines and the advantage of iron scrap and HCl.
Explain ammonolysis of alkyl halides and why it gives a mixture of amines.
Apply Gabriel phthalimide synthesis and Hoffmann bromamide degradation to prepare primary amines.
Relate the boiling points of amines to intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
Explain the solubility of amines in water in terms of hydrogen bonding and the alkyl part.
Interpret Kb and pKb values to compare the basic strength of amines.
Explain the order of basicity of alkylamines from inductive, solvation and steric effects.
Explain why arylamines are weaker bases than ammonia and how substituents change this.

topics.title: Alkylation, acylation and tests for amines

concepts.learning_objective: Describe acylation and benzoylation of primary and secondary amines.
Use the carbylamine reaction and the reaction with nitrous acid to identify primary amines.
Distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary amines with benzenesulphonyl chloride.
Explain the ortho/para directing and activating effect of the amino group.
Explain how acetylation controls the reactivity of aniline in substitution.
Explain meta product in nitration, sulphonation and failure of Friedel-Crafts reaction of aniline.
Describe the preparation of benzenediazonium chloride by diazotisation.
Explain the stability of arenediazonium salts compared with alkyldiazonium salts.

topics.title: Reactions of diazonium salts and their importance in synthesis

concepts.learning_objective: Describe replacement of the diazonium group by halide, cyanide, hydroxyl, hydrogen and nitro groups.
Describe coupling reactions of diazonium salts with phenol and aniline to form azo compounds.
Plan syntheses of aromatic compounds that cannot be made by direct substitution.
Define carbohydrates chemically and classify them as monosaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides by their behaviour on hydrolysis.
Name monosaccharides as aldoses or ketoses by carbon number and recognise that all monosaccharides are reducing sugars.
Relate the reactions of glucose to the evidence for its open-chain structure.
Explain the cyclic hemiacetal (pyranose) structure of glucose and its alpha and beta anomers.
Interpret the D/L and (+)/(-) notation of sugars with reference to glyceraldehyde.

topics.title: Disaccharides, polysaccharides and importance of carbohydrates

concepts.learning_objective: Describe glycosidic linkages in sucrose, maltose and lactose and decide whether a disaccharide is reducing.
Explain the change in sign of rotation on hydrolysis of sucrose (invert sugar).
Compare the structures of starch (amylose, amylopectin), cellulose and glycogen.

topics.title: Amino acids and structure of proteins

concepts.learning_objective: Classify amino acids as acidic, basic or neutral and as essential or non-essential.
Explain the zwitter ion form and the salt-like, amphoteric behaviour of amino acids.
Describe peptide bond formation and the primary to quaternary levels of protein structure.
Explain denaturation of proteins and its effect on their structure and activity.
Describe enzymes as specific biocatalysts that lower activation energy, and how they are named.
Classify vitamins as fat soluble or water soluble and relate this to their storage in the body.
Match important vitamins with their sources and deficiency diseases.
State the sugars, bases and phosphate units of DNA and RNA and distinguish nucleosides from nucleotides.
Apply complementary base pairing in the DNA double helix.
Describe the roles of DNA and RNA in heredity and protein synthesis.
Classify hormones as steroids, polypeptides or amino acid derivatives.
Relate common hormones and glands to their functions and to disorders of deficiency or excess.
